newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran, Turkey, Turkmenistan to discuss energy deals.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Turkey, Turkmenistan to discuss energy deals.

text.p: Ministers from Iran, Turkey and Turkmenistan will convene in Tehran over the weekend to discuss gas and other energy projects, a Turkish energy ministry statement said on Friday.

It said Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan had left Ankara for Tehran to attend the talks which are expected to focus on a multi-billion-dollar deal to carry Turkmen gas to Turkey and Europe through a pipeline.
The talks are expected to revive the pipeline project which was proposed in early 1995 but later dropped due to financial difficulties and U.S. reservations over Iran's involvement.
The revised project requires Turkey to build a 400-km (250-mile) line to link to an existing line from Turkmenistan to Georgia, bypassing Iran.

Turkey signed a landmark 23-year, $23-billion agreement with Iran in August to buy an initial three billion cubic metres of gas a year from 1998 through a pipeline, to be built by Turkey and Iran on their own territories.
